recent_posts.title: Merry Christmas, Ya Filthy Animals (2025) — Ludicity
recent_posts.summary: A personal reflection on running a software consultancy, embracing uncertainty, and building an ethical business. The author discusses mortality, generosity, accepting help from others, and plans to grow their team while maintaining human-oriented values. They aim to compete against incompetent or unethical competitors by documenting a replicable blueprint for running a principled consulting business that compensates people fairly.

recent_posts.title: Escaping corporate dysfunction by starting an independent consulting business
recent_posts.summary: A software professional reflects on successfully starting a consulting business after years of corporate frustration. The author discusses the hidden divide between dysfunctional and high-functioning tech companies, why conventional job search advice often fails, and how quitting into unemployment can paradoxically lead to better opportunities. Key insights include the accessibility of independent consulting work, the psychological barriers preventing people from leaving bad jobs, and how autonomy fundamentally changes one's relationship with work and earning potential.

recent_posts.title: Challenging claims about AI programming productivity and ethics
recent_posts.summary: A detailed critique of Thomas Ptacek's pro-AI article, challenging claims about AI programming productivity gains and questioning the ethics of AI training on open source code. The author argues that current AI hype exceeds realistic benefits, criticizes dismissive attitudes toward licensing concerns, and suggests that anecdotal evidence of dramatic productivity improvements lacks substantiation. The piece also examines the disconnect between AI marketing promises and actual developer experiences.

recent_posts.title: The Narrative Fallacy — Ludicity
recent_posts.summary: Narratives make weak arguments and flawed research appear compelling by providing coherent stories that bypass critical thinking. The author examines how storytelling acts as a symmetric persuasion tool that works regardless of truth, using examples from psychology research, political commentary, and academic grading. Universities inadvertently reinforce this problem by rewarding narrative-driven essays over rigorous analysis, creating a system where compelling stories matter more than factual accuracy. The piece advocates for recognizing when narratives obscure rather than illuminate understanding.

recent_posts.title: Influence of book covers and unconventional career choices
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the influence of book cover design on reader perception and sales, highlighting Ursula K. Le Guin's experiences with mismatched cover art. It critiques the conservatism in publishing and other industries, where conformity is often valued over creativity. The author shares personal insights into the challenges of being different in both publishing and entrepreneurship, emphasizing the importance of conviction in one's judgment and the courage to deviate from norms.

recent_posts.title: A guide to securing software engineering jobs
recent_posts.summary: This post offers a comprehensive guide on securing software engineering jobs, drawing from personal success and industry insights. It emphasizes the importance of setting high standards for job satisfaction and respect in the workplace. The author discusses the advantages of contracting over full-time positions, the relevance of a well-optimized CV filled with relevant buzzwords, and the necessity of effective networking. The post also highlights the significance of confidence, self-respect, and being resourceful and unorthodox in job searching strategies.

recent_posts.title: The influence of marketing on executive decisions
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the author's experience with a Chief Technology Officer who, despite being highly regarded, relied heavily on marketing and buzzwords rather than genuine technical understanding. It highlights the susceptibility of executives to marketing tactics and the consequences of such influence on decision-making in large organizations. The narrative reveals the broader implications of having suggestible leaders in positions of power and the interplay of status and ineffective management in the tech industry.

recent_posts.title: Merry Christmas, Ya Filthy Animals (2024) — Ludicity
recent_posts.summary: The author shares reflections on quitting their job, the benefits of pursuing consulting work, and the joy of having more time to focus on personal interests. Despite a busy schedule, the author is committed to writing more frequently and has ambitious goals for 2025, including working on two book projects and improving their technical skills and musical performance. They emphasize the importance of growth, community, and aligning personal goals with professional work.

recent_posts.title: The Importance of Quality and Meaning in Software Engineering
recent_posts.summary: The author expresses frustration with the inefficiencies and lack of meaningful work in the software engineering sector, recounting experiences that led them to start their own consultancy. Reflecting on generational attitudes towards risk and work, the piece contrasts cynicism and gratitude, ultimately advocating for a proactive approach to effecting positive change. The author underscores the importance of quality in various aspects of life, from software engineering practices to healthcare systems.

recent_posts.title: Navigating the complexities of enterprise data systems
recent_posts.summary: An engineer describes their experience working with a convoluted enterprise data warehouse platform. Despite the team's camaraderie, the environment is fraught with technical issues and poor management practices. After navigating persistent problems like corrupted logs and ineffective data processing, the author decides to resign to focus on more meaningful and productive work.
